title: Issue is whether application is faith-act or only fiducia-act (Vasquez names it faith)
source_text: LXVIII. Itaque quaestio non est, An fidelis possit & debeat gratiae promissiones sibi applicare, sed an applicatio ista sit fidei actus? quod tenent Reformati: An vero non fidei, sed fiduciae tantum actus censeri debeat? quae est sententia Doctorum Ecclesiae Romanae. Et tamen inter ipsos Ecclesiae Romanae Doctores non desunt qui istam persuasionem, quam fidelis aliquis concipit de gratia Dei, sive jam obtenta, sive in futurum obtinenda, fidei nomine donent, quo de numero esse Gabrielem Vasquez Jesuita manifestum faciunt quae supra ex ipso allata fuerunt.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore the question is not whether a believer can and ought to apply the promises of grace to himself, but whether that application is an act of faith — which the Reformed hold — or whether it ought to be counted not as an act of faith but only of trust — which is the opinion of the Doctors of the Roman Church. And yet among the Doctors of the Roman Church themselves there are not wanting those who give the name of faith to that persuasion which some believer conceives about God grace, whether already obtained or to be obtained in the future, of which number Gabriel Vasquez the Jesuit is shown to be by what was brought forward from him above.
pass_b_english: The real question is not whether the believer may/should apply grace promises, but whether that application is a faith-act (Reformed) or only a fiducia-act (Rome).
Even so, some Romans including Vasquez still name that persuasion about obtained or future grace as faith.

lemmas.latin: an applicatio ista sit fidei actus
lemmas.gloss: whether that application is an act of faith

choices.why: Classification fight; Vasquez blurs Rome side.
rejected: Rome unanimously denies any faith-name to the persuasion
